text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The government continues its attack against those who avoid paying taxes. The tax inspection will pay closer attention to companies which pay salaries below 500 litas.
- Deputy prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas officially announced his intention stand as president.

- Lithuania has made big progress on its way to the European Union although it still has to do a lot to reach EU standards, said EU Commissioner Hans Van Den Broek after a meeting with President Algirdas Brazauskas.
- Lithuanian Social Democrats may launch a referendum on the privatisation of key companies in the communication, energy and transport sectors.
- Parliament's economy committee doubts the competence of the finance ministry to run the privatisation of two state-run banks.
- Construction works volume decreased by 8.7 percent in 1996.
- The defence ministers of three Baltic countries met in Vilnius to decide on co-ordination of joint projects.
- The most active stocks on the Vilnius bourse during the first quarter of 1997 were Rokishkis Cheese, Lithuanian Gas, Sanitas, Ukio Bank and Hermis bank.
- After the liquidation of Innovation bank the Lithuanian government will have to decide what to do with 3.8 tonnes of beryllium stored in the bank.
- The government stopped the nine percent value added tax subsidies to bread and products from April 1.
- Historian Jonas Rekeshius was appointed new spokesman for President Brazauskas.
